text: {"features":[{"name":"Role targeting","description":"How specifically the letter is tailored to this Google Information Security Engineering role rather than to a generic software job.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"The letter could apply to many software roles and gives little indication that the writer understands this specific team or job."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"The letter names the role or team and gives one broad reason for interest, but the fit still feels mostly generic."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"The letter clearly connects the applicant's background to at least one major responsibility or qualification in the posting."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"The letter ties several posted responsibilities or qualifications to past work and explains why this team is an especially good fit."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"The letter feels unmistakably written for this exact role, linking Google's scale, the security mission, and the Go plus Python automation work to the applicant's background."}]},{"name":"Security systems thinking","description":"How well the letter shows an understanding of security work as a systems problem that can be scaled with automation and infrastructure.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"The letter shows little or no understanding of security work as a systems or scale problem."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"The letter mentions security or automation in broad terms without showing the underlying scaling challenge."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"The letter recognizes that tooling can reduce manual security toil or make secure behavior easier by default."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"The letter clearly frames security work as a capacity or workflow problem and cites relevant experience addressing it."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"The letter articulates a strong role-relevant view of scaling scarce security judgment through automation such as triage, variant analysis, or centrally provided developer tooling."}]},{"name":"Production software track record","description":"How strong the letter's evidence is that the applicant has substantial real-world experience testing, maintaining, and launching production software.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"The letter shows only a narrow version of the minimum experience, such as a few years and very few production services."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"The letter shows early-career production experience with some maintenance, testing, and launch exposure but limited breadth."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"The letter shows solid production experience across several years or multiple services with clear ownership."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"The letter shows substantial production ownership through repeated launches, maintenance, and operation of several services."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"The letter shows deep and sustained production experience across many years and services, conveying readiness to contribute immediately in a high-leverage environment."}]},{"name":"Academic preparation","description":"How strong the formal academic preparation is that the letter presents for a systems-heavy security engineering role.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"The letter presents only a bachelor's degree as baseline qualification, with no sign of advanced academic depth."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"The letter presents a relevant bachelor's degree and adds some explicit sign of stronger formal depth, such as research, advanced coursework, or similarly theory-heavy framing."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"The letter presents a relevant master's degree or comparable advanced study."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"The letter presents a relevant doctoral degree or other research-level training."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"The letter presents research-level academic depth and explicitly connects it to the analytical demands of the role."}]},{"name":"Go expertise","description":"How convincingly the letter shows depth of professional experience using Go for the kinds of back-end systems this role requires.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"The letter mentions Go only as one language in the background with no further evidence of depth."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"The letter states that Go is a primary or daily language but gives no role-relevant example of using it."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"The letter shows clear professional use of Go in production services or backend work."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"The letter ties Go to design or operation of substantial backend or security infrastructure."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"The letter makes Go central to architecting the kind of controlled, role-relevant backend systems this team builds."}]},{"name":"Python expertise","description":"How convincingly the letter shows depth of Python experience for automation, services, or AI-agent work relevant to the role.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"The letter omits Python or mentions it only in passing."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"The letter states Python experience in general terms without showing scope or type of work."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"The letter describes regular Python use for services, tooling, or automation."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"The letter shows strong production Python use, such as major automation layers or typed and tested internal services."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"The letter makes Python central to highly relevant work such as security automation, analysis systems, or AI agents in production."}]},{"name":"Agentic tooling design","description":"How much the letter demonstrates hands-on design of agent-based systems, especially with explicit controls around what agents can do.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"The letter gives no evidence of experience with agents or autonomous tooling."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"The letter mentions agents or automation loosely without enough architectural detail to judge depth."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"The letter clearly describes building agent-based tooling or systems with identifiable components."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"The letter shows end-to-end agent design with explicit boundaries, permissions, supervision, or auditability."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"The letter presents agentic architecture as a major strength, with deliberate delegation to agents and equally deliberate control infrastructure around them."}]},{"name":"Vulnerability handling automation","description":"How much the letter shows direct experience automating vulnerability intake, triage, routing, or related response workflows.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"The letter gives no evidence of automating vulnerability intake, triage, or response workflows."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"The letter expresses interest in automating security toil but cites no concrete vulnerability-handling work."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"The letter describes some direct work on automating vulnerability reports, intake, or triage."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"The letter shows clear ownership of classification, routing, deduplication, prioritization, or similar workflow automation that reduced manual effort."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"The letter shows strong end-to-end vulnerability-handling automation that materially expanded team capacity or made the process largely self-serve."}]},{"name":"Security assessment capability","description":"How convincingly the letter shows ability to perform security assessments of designs or running systems.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"The letter gives no evidence of performing security assessments."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"The letter mentions threat models, reviews, or assessments only in generic terms."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"The letter clearly states experience performing security assessments or security reviews of designs or services."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"The letter shows hands-on assessment work with concrete methods such as attacker-minded review, threat modeling, or remediation validation."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"The letter shows repeated, structured assessment work across multiple systems or stages of development, conveying strong judgment rather than checklist compliance."}]},{"name":"AI application experience","description":"How much the letter demonstrates practical experience building and operating AI-backed functionality in production.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"The letter gives no evidence of AI or machine-learning work."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"The letter mentions AI in broad or aspirational terms without clear hands-on production use."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"The letter shows clear hands-on AI or LLM experience in shipped features, workflows, or tooling."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"The letter shows production AI experience paired with attention to reliability, evaluation, or safeguards."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"The letter shows substantial role-relevant AI experience that combines shipping, hardening, and trustworthy operation of AI-backed systems."}]},{"name":"Algorithmic problem solving","description":"How convincingly the letter shows strong applied computational reasoning through algorithm or data-structure choices.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"The letter gives no evidence of using algorithmic or data-structure choices to solve real problems."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"The letter claims comfort with algorithmic work but provides no concrete example."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"The letter gives one clear example of improving a system through a better algorithm or structure choice."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"The letter shows strong applied algorithmic thinking through substantial examples tied to performance, scale, or system tractability."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"The letter presents algorithmic reasoning as a standout strength central to solving hard, high-volume engineering problems."}]},{"name":"Developer enablement mindset","description":"How strongly the letter presents security tooling as a way to help other engineers move faster and more safely, not just to enforce rules.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"The letter frames the work mainly as building software in isolation and says little about helping other engineers."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"The letter briefly mentions helping teams or improving security defaults without much substance."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"The letter clearly values tooling that makes other engineers more effective or more secure by default."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"The letter repeatedly emphasizes reducing friction, returning time, or embedding secure behavior into everyday development workflows."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"The letter makes downstream engineer success the core measure of impact and describes security tooling primarily as an enabling service to others."}]},{"name":"External security practice","description":"How much the letter shows deliberate security skill-building beyond ordinary job duties through CTFs, certifications, or similar practice.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"The letter mentions no security practice, certification, or offensive learning outside ordinary job duties."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"The letter offers one modest signal, such as a basic certification or casual competition participation."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"The letter shows a stronger single signal, such as sustained CTF participation or a demanding certification like OSCP."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"The letter shows multiple strong signals, such as serious competition results plus certification or other sustained offensive practice."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"The letter shows unusually strong external security credibility through a combination of difficult validation, serious competition performance, and clear deliberate skill-building."}]},{"name":"Self-driven engineering initiative","description":"How much the letter shows meaningful engineering work pursued beyond assigned responsibilities, such as side projects, upstream fixes, or open-source stewardship.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"The letter gives no evidence of meaningful engineering work beyond assigned job responsibilities."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"The letter mentions a small side project or light tinkering with limited scope or persistence."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"The letter shows concrete initiative beyond work through a sustained side project, occasional upstream fixes, or comparable effort."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"The letter demonstrates substantial self-driven engineering through ambitious personal systems, recurring upstream contributions, or open-source ownership."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"The letter shows exceptional initiative beyond work, such as stewardship of a widely used open-source project or a combination of serious community maintenance and ambitious systems building."}]},{"name":"Evidence specificity","description":"How concrete and observable the supporting evidence is for the claims made in the letter.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"The letter relies mostly on broad claims or adjectives and offers almost no concrete examples, technologies, or actions."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"The letter includes a few specific nouns or tools but leaves most major claims unsubstantiated."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"The letter gives several concrete examples of work, though some important claims remain general."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"The letter consistently backs important claims with specific tasks, technologies, or situations."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"The letter grounds nearly every major claim in concrete, observable detail that makes the applicant's work easy to picture and trust."}]},{"name":"Impact articulation","description":"How clearly the letter explains the outcomes or value created by the applicant's work.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"The letter lists activities without explaining what changed, improved, or mattered."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"The letter suggests usefulness but gives little explicit sense of outcome, scale, or consequence."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"The letter states clear outcomes such as reduced toil, faster systems, better routing, or improved reliability."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"The letter links multiple examples to meaningful outcomes for teams, systems, or security operations."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"The letter makes impact vivid and credible by showing how the work changed capacity, reliability, or security at meaningful scale, sometimes with a concrete measure or especially clear causal framing."}]},{"name":"Narrative flow","description":"How clearly the letter is structured so its points build into a persuasive case.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"The letter feels disjointed or hard to follow, with weak progression between points."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"The letter has a basic structure but still reads as choppy, stitched together, or overly list-like."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"The letter is generally easy to follow, with a recognizable opening, body, and close."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"The letter flows smoothly from motivation to qualifications to evidence, with ideas building naturally."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"The letter has an especially strong narrative arc that makes the case feel cumulative, coherent, and easy to remember."}]},{"name":"Mechanical polish","description":"How free the letter is from spelling, grammar, and typographical errors.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"The letter contains frequent spelling, grammar, or typographical errors that repeatedly distract from the message."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"The letter contains several noticeable errors or awkward constructions that interrupt reading even though the meaning stays clear."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"The letter has a few errors or rough spots but remains professionally readable overall."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"The letter is clean and professional with only minor blemishes, if any."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"The letter is essentially error-free and polished at a very high standard."}]}]}
